name: java-security
description: trigger: writing Java or Kotlin (Spring, Jakarta EE, Quarkus, Android), SQL/JPA/MyBatis, templates, application.properties/.yml, web.xml, pom.xml, Gradle; "customize java security" opens the guided page. avoid: injection, XXE, SSRF, unsafe deserialization, path traversal, weak crypto, trust-all TLS, Spring Security off, exposed secrets, known-exploited deps, SpotBugs/Sonar/PMD/Checkstyle findings. 129 rules, 16 packs, each allow|deny|ask in .chock/security.json; absent = deny (quality: allow). [Session-enforced via PreToolUse and Stop hooks; needs git and a Python 3.11+. PreToolUse judges the file a tool call would write; Stop re-reads what the turn actually left on disk, so a file written through a shell heredoc is judged too. With no working Python the hook exits 2; without git, fail-open clients allow silently. A gate that cannot reach a decision refuses rather than allowing one it never judged. Enforcement at every commit and in CI still needs chock installed in the repo.]
